title: Network Analysis, PERT and CPM (PMT 801)
subject: Project management
description: Thirty questions across easy, medium and hard on Gantt charts, CPM, PERT time estimates, critical paths, float and project completion probability, with a few short calculations.

questions.prompt: Which two network methods are popularly used?
options: The Critical Path Method (CPM) and the Program Evaluation and Review Technique (PERT)
PERT and the nominal group method
questions.explanation: Gantt or bar charts were used before the formal development of network planning.

questions.prompt: What is scheduling in network analysis?
options: Developing a timetable by putting time estimates alongside the developed plan
Establishing objectives and defining the content of the project
Following up, updating and reporting progress
questions.explanation: Planning shows what activities are to be done, and scheduling adds time.

questions.prompt: What is project control, according to the lecture?
options: The process of defining the project's objectives
A follow-up, updating and reporting process that makes events conform to schedules
questions.explanation: It is regarded as the third major element of project management.

questions.prompt: Who introduced Gantt charts in network planning?
questions.explanation: Gantt charts were widely used before the formal development of network planning.

questions.prompt: Which items does a Gantt chart include?
options: The probability of completion and standard deviation
A listing of activities, activity duration, schedule dates and project status
questions.explanation: Each line on the chart represents a single activity.

questions.prompt: PERT was first used in the 1950s to manage which programme?
questions.explanation: It has since been used in construction, major maintenance, pilot production runs and new product introduction.

questions.prompt: Which is the PERT formula for expected time?
questions.explanation: The most likely time m is the most heavily weighted.

questions.prompt: In PERT time estimates, what does a stand for?
questions.explanation: m is the most likely time and b is the pessimistic time.

questions.prompt: What does a dummy arrow represent?
options: A job with the longest duration
A relationship between jobs, with no activity, no resource use and no duration
questions.explanation: Dummy arrows are drawn as dashed lines.

questions.prompt: What does the duration of a project equal?
options: The sum of all activity times
The time required on the critical path
The duration of the shortest path
The average of all path durations
questions.explanation: The critical path is the longest path through the network.

questions.prompt: What is the fundamental difference between CPM and PERT?
options: CPM is cost conscious and uses single deterministic estimates, while PERT is time conscious and uses three probabilistic estimates
CPM is time conscious and uses three estimates, while PERT is cost conscious and uses one
CPM uses probabilities, while PERT uses fixed times
There is no difference between them
questions.explanation: The network principles of both are alike.

questions.prompt: Which is an advantage of network analysis over Gantt charts?
options: It removes the need for time estimates
It does not show relationships between activities
It enhances inter-departmental communication and focuses on critical tasks
It works only for small projects
questions.explanation: It also permits alternative methods, clear definition of responsibilities and fewer crises.

questions.prompt: When is deterministic PERT suited?
options: When no time estimates are possible
When tasks are routine and the time for each is known with reasonable certainty, such as repair and maintenance
questions.explanation: Even though each task is routine, the project may comprise many of them.

questions.prompt: Why is stochastic PERT used for research or one-of-a-kind development projects?
options: Task durations cannot be estimated precisely, so a range of estimates is used, often from expert advice
questions.explanation: The act of identifying milestones and logical links also gives valuable insight.

questions.prompt: Which techniques are used to obtain and assimilate expert advice for stochastic PERT?
options: The Delphi method and the nominal group method
questions.explanation: These are the most frequently used techniques when advice must come from a panel of experts.

questions.prompt: How is the standard deviation of an activity's time assumed in PERT?
options: One-third of the most likely time
One-sixth of the range between the optimistic and pessimistic times
The difference between the most likely and optimistic times
questions.explanation: That is why the formula is (b minus a) divided by 6.

questions.prompt: In the PERT estimate, which time is weighted most heavily?
questions.explanation: The result is a weighted average of the time the activity would take if repeated many times.

questions.prompt: Which is a step in preparing a bar chart?
options: Place activities on a time sequence, knowing some must be done in sequence and others can be done at the same time
Calculate the IRR of each activity
questions.explanation: If a completion date is specified, the diagram is adjusted until it is satisfied.

questions.prompt: What does it mean for activities to be in series?
options: B can proceed while A is still going
Activity A must be completed before activity B can start
A and B share the same resources
A and B have no relationship
questions.explanation: Activities in parallel can proceed at the same time.

questions.prompt: How is the activity to crash chosen?
options: The activity with the most float
The activity with the highest cost
By the least cost, using time and cost trade-offs, usually on the critical path
questions.explanation: Crashing can create another critical path if the days crashed exceed the free float on another path.

questions.prompt: An activity has an optimistic time of 2 days, a most likely time of 4 days and a pessimistic time of 12 days. What is its expected time?
An activity has an optimistic time of 3 days and a pessimistic time of 15 days. What is its standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Standard deviation = (b minus a) / 6 = (15 - 3) / 6 = 2 days.

questions.prompt: The paths of a network are ACFI (12.14), ADGI (11.47), ADH (8.5), BEGI (11.97) and BEH (9). Which is the critical path and why?
options: ADH, because it has the shortest duration
BEH, because it has the fewest activities
ACFI, because it has the longest duration
BEGI, because it begins with activity B
questions.explanation: The critical path is the longest path and sets the project duration.

questions.prompt: In an activity table, activity G has immediate predecessor E. What does this mean?
options: G is finished before E starts
G and E are the same activity
G cannot start until E is complete
questions.explanation: Immediate predecessors show the order in which activities must be done.

questions.prompt: What happens if a non-critical activity is delayed longer than its slack?
questions.explanation: Variation in non-critical activities normally has no effect on duration because of their slack.

questions.prompt: Which is a correct way to find the total float of an activity?
options: Latest finish time minus earliest finish time
Earliest start time minus earliest finish time
Earliest finish time minus latest start time
questions.explanation: The lecture gives total float as latest finish minus earliest finish. A float of zero means the activity is critical.

questions.prompt: In the factory power plant example, what is the total float of the critical activities A, B, H, I, K, L and M?
questions.explanation: Critical activities have no slack, and they are marked with an asterisk in the table.

questions.prompt: A project's critical path is expected to take 40 days with a variance of 16 days squared. If the deadline is 44 days, what is the approximate chance of finishing on time?
questions.explanation: The standard deviation is the square root of 16, which is 4. Z = (44 - 40) / 4 = 1, which corresponds to about 84 percent on the standard normal table.

questions.prompt: How is the variance of the critical path obtained?
options: By adding the variances of the activities on the critical path
By averaging the variances of all activities
By adding the variances of every path
By taking the largest single variance
questions.explanation: Only the critical activities are included, because the critical path determines project duration.

questions.prompt: A project team works 6 days a week and the deadline is 14 weeks. How many working days are available?
questions.explanation: 14 weeks multiplied by 6 days gives 84 working days.
